name: Genetic Visceral Malformation of the Liver, Biliary Tract, Pancreas or Spleen

criteria.description: Presence of congenital malformation affecting one or more of the liver, biliary tract, pancreas, or spleen confirmed by imaging or surgical findings
Positive family history of similar visceral malformations or known genetic mutation
Identification of pathogenic variant in genes associated with visceral organ development
Clinical symptoms consistent with visceral malformation such as cholestasis, pancreatitis, or splenomegaly

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital visceral anomaly plus either family history or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by imaging and laboratory findings consistent with organ dysfunction.

pathognomonic.notes: Fibrotic changes in liver tissue evident on biopsy or imaging
searchTerms: fibrous liver tissue present at birth

pathognomonic.notes: Abnormal bile duct architecture leading to cholestasis
Congenital structural abnormalities of pancreatic ducts

common.notes: Yellowing of skin and sclera due to bile flow obstruction
Enlargement of the spleen detected clinically or by imaging
Episodes of pancreatic inflammation due to ductal malformations
Enlarged liver on physical exam or imaging

occasional.notes: Elevated pressure in portal venous system secondary to liver malformation
Impaired digestion and absorption of dietary fats
Persistent pain related to organ malformations

rare.notes: Localized tissue death in spleen due to vascular compromise
Reduced pancreatic enzyme production causing maldigestion
Progressive liver scarring due to chronic bile duct obstruction

laboratory: Elevated liver enzymes (ALT, AST, ALP, GGT)
Cholestatic pattern of liver function tests
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing hepatic fibrosis and biliary ductal anomalies
CT or MRI demonstrating pancreatic duct malformations
Splenomegaly and portal hypertension on Doppler ultrasound
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes regulating visceral organ development (e.g., PKHD1, JAG1)
Familial inheritance patterns consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive transmission
other: Histopathology confirming congenital hepatic fibrosis or biliary duct paucity
Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) showing ductal abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of bile ducts on imaging
Segmental dilatation of intrahepatic bile ducts

redFlags: Severe portal hypertension with variceal bleeding
